canonical.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm — Negative Weights and Cycles
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/08. Bellman Ford Algorithm.cpp

narrative.title: Auditing Rebate Loops in the Settlement Grid
narrative.scenario: A settlement grid routes money between accounts over channels that may carry rebates — negative costs. The finance desk must know each account's cheapest receivable total from the clearing house, but a loop of rebates that keeps shrinking its own payout poisons the books. Bellman-Ford answers both: the cheapest totals, or a hard alarm if such a rebate loop exists.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer V (vertices 0..V-1), an edge list edges where [u, v, w] is a one-way channel u -> v with cost w (possibly negative), and the source S.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the array of shortest distances from S, or the single-element array [-1] if a negative cycle is reachable from S.

testCases.explanation: Node 0 is reached by 2 -> 0 costing 1; node 1 rides through 0 for 6.
A single channel settles both accounts immediately.

hintLevels: Level 1: Repeatedly let every channel try to improve every account's total — patience replaces the priority queue.
Level 2: V-1 full relaxation sweeps suffice because a shortest path visits at most V-1 channels.
Level 3: A sweep V that still improves some distance certifies a shrinking loop — emit the alarm array.
